title: Code Reviewer hardened Worker container, version 1
description: The hardened container spec (#316, #318): one definition of the flags of the container a Worker runs in, so that the self-hosted compose files and the container the Sandbox-Launcher starts inside a VM cannot drift apart. The schema is the hardening floor: a document that weakens it (privileged, a bind or volume, a device, host namespaces, host networking, an unconfined seccomp or AppArmor profile, a writable root, a weaker tmpfs, another user, another capability set, a credential in the environment) is refused, because the weakening has no key to live in or a value the schema does not allow. examples/worker-container/WorkerContainerSpec.json is the spec and equals compose.dynamic.yml and the runner-dynamic service of compose.coolify.yml (tests in the app, #325 extends them); the renderer to `docker run` arguments is #325. Per Worker kind a launcher may override only what WorkerContainerOverrides names (the memory limit: the self-hosted default is the spec's, the Sandbox sizes differ). The per-job credential is never part of a container: it goes to the Worker on stdin.

MemorySize.description: A size in the notation of docker: digits and m or g.

Capability.description: The capabilities the Worker container may be created with, nothing else. SETUID SETGID KILL CHOWN DAC_OVERRIDE FOWNER stay for the life of the container (the root supervisor starts the engine as another user, seals and removes its tree); NET_ADMIN and SETPCAP are startup only: the entry point installs the engine user's static network rules and then drops both from every set, including the bounding set, before any job exists.

startupOnly.description: true exactly for NET_ADMIN and SETPCAP.

TmpfsMount.description: A private memory filesystem. It can run no program, honour no setuid bit and hold no device; it is charged to the memory limit, hence the sizes.

SecurityOption.description: no-new-privileges, or a named seccomp profile (never `unconfined`). No other option: AppArmor and SELinux labels are the daemon's.

EnvironmentName.description: A name the container may be given. Never one that looks like it holds a secret: the dispatcher token and the per-job credential do not reach a container through its environment.

swap.description: Memory plus swap. Equal to the limit: no swap, so the peak shows as an out-of-memory kill of the job.

ForbiddenKey.description: A key a spec never has, and the renderer never emits.

user.description: The container starts as root: the job process of a Dynamic job is the supervisor that owns every credential and starts the engine as another user. Root holds exactly the capabilities of capAdd and no-new-privileges means nothing can regain more.

network.description: The default bridge. Never the host's network and never none (the Worker must reach the app).

forbiddenKeys.description: Documentation that a tool can check: the keys that no spec has. The schema is closed, so none of them can be added.

overridable.description: The only values a launcher may change per Worker kind (WorkerContainerOverrides).

WorkerContainerOverrides.description: What a launcher may change per Worker kind (ADR of the hosted deployment, #325): the memory limit, because the self-hosted default is not the size of a Sandbox VM. Nothing else.
